attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Dermatology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
7-month history of worsening acne on face, chest, and upper back unresponsive to over-the-counter cleansers

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient presents for dermatologic evaluation eight months following her diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome. She reports that over-the-counter cleansers have not helped.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Polycystic ovary syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Insulin resistance
- Overweight (BMI 29 kg/m²)

She is otherwise healthy.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- None

MEDICATIONS:
She takes no other medications.

Home Medications:
- Metformin 500 mg orally twice daily
- Calcium carbonate with vitamin D 600 mg/400 units orally once daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed age 42)
- Maternal aunt: Polycystic ovary syndrome
- Father: Dyslipidemia

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: University undergraduate student.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
She has regular menstrual cycles

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, she has multiple inflammatory papules and pustules with scattered closed comedones over the cheeks and jawline, with mild hyperpigmented scars. There are no signs of virilization.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
Six weeks later, the patient reports significant improvement in her skin lesions.

The physician prescribes an oral medication that is suitable for case severity.
She is counseled on avoiding pregnancy during treatment due to the risk of teratogenicity.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-05-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Dermatology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Worsening facial acne with pain and scarring despite 6 months of topical and oral antibiotic therapy

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 20-year-old female with polycystic ovary syndrome, insulin resistance, and overweight status (BMI 29 kg/m²) returns to the dermatology clinic for follow-up of acne initially evaluated in September 2020. She presents with a 6-month history of worsening facial acne. She reports that the acne is painful and has been associated with scarring. She has tried multiple topical treatments including benzoyl peroxide and adapalene, as well as oral antibiotics, without significant improvement. She expresses significant distress about her appearance and is eager for more effective treatment.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Polycystic ovary syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Acne vulgaris (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Insulin resistance
- Overweight (BMI 29 kg/m²)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- None

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Metformin 500 mg orally twice daily
- Calcium carbonate with vitamin D 600 mg/400 units orally once daily

ALLERGIES:
She has no known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed age 42)
- Maternal aunt: Polycystic ovary syndrome
- Father: Dyslipidemia

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She denies using any hormonal contraceptives and is currently sexually active with one partner, using condoms inconsistently.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, she has numerous erythematous nodules and cysts on her face, some with evidence of scarring.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory values:
- Liver function tests: Within normal limits
- Lipid panel:
- Total cholesterol: 185 mg/dL
- HDL: 55 mg/dL
- LDL: 100 mg/dL
- Triglycerides: 150 mg/dL
- Urine pregnancy test: Negative
